overall_summary: Analysis of FACTVERSE performance data highlights clear audience preference for high-concept, extreme space scenarios ('What If' hypotheticals and bizarre exoplanet conditions) over general psychological or historical facts. Videos exploring extreme planetary environments (e.g., diamond planets, burning ice planets, dark planets) generated the highest views-per-day and engagement (likes-per-view), particularly when framed around visceral sensory experiences or hypothetical viewer immersion.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Exoplanet Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) achieved high view velocity (over 900+ views within days) and strong engagement (up to 38 likes).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If' immersion formats focusing on extreme, visually striking celestial bodies not yet covered.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing extreme phenomena such as supersonic rubies (QXuqYERlqSo) or dark-than-coal compositions (v1rrcZLdp4U) consistently outperform standard trivia with 700-1000+ views.
winning_patterns.action: Continue producing short-form segments on extreme cosmic anomalies with shocking physical properties.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (Jc04LVKNd2s) stalled below 20-55 views with zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract psychological micro-facts unless they involve a high-impact, bizarre visual experiment or extreme human survival scenario.

weak_patterns.evidence: Items like 'The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery Science Can't Solve' (yLm-FjYH6-k) or basic biology facts (Octopuses, Sharks) underperformed relative to cosmic horror and extreme space topics in recent windows.
weak_patterns.action: Shift focus away from standard historical trivia and reallocate production capacity toward high-concept space and cinematic survival.

next_video.concept: What happens if you fall into a star made entirely of liquid neon?
next_video.opening_direction: Start mid-action with the sound of a cracking glass hull and instant freezing darkness.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the neon core doesn't burn you with heat, but shatters your body via extreme cryogenic pressure before you even touch the surface.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performing 'What If' exoplanet/cosmic body framework while introducing a completely fresh scientific element (liquid neon stars) absent from past uploads.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not feature diamonds, glass rain, or burning ice.
Must focus on a newly introduced celestial anomaly.
Must maintain strict scientific accuracy regarding extreme states of matter.

experiment: Test a 15-second pacing structure with a zero-second cold open (direct drop into the hypothetical scenario) compared to standard 21-second narrative builds to measure impact on audience retention and like-to-view ratios.
